description: 8-week course teaching the core skills of improv via weekly themed exercises (spontaneity, confidence, listening, commitment) plus warm-ups and short scenes/games; no prior experience required.

exercise_name: Yes And / Listen / Commit core drills
description: Foundational improv agreement and active-listening drills built on the school's three principles (Listen, Yes And, Commit); students build on each other's offers in pairs and groups.
8-week course that gently introduces performing improv comedy live in front of an audience for the first time, culminating in an end-of-course show of short-form games and scenes.
8-week course focused on improvising character- and relationship-driven scenes, with a performance at the end.
8-week course exploring longer scenes in depth and connecting scenes to explore themes and patterns across time and space, with an end-of-course performance.

exercise_name: Advanced Improv specializations (The Harold, Deconstruction, etc.)
description: Level 5 advanced workshops in named long-form structures and styles: improvised theatre, improvised narrative, improvised movies, character, Harolds, deconstruction, commedia, clown, stagecraft, solo improv, and improvised musicals.
Flexible single-session practice workshops to keep improvising between or alongside courses; mixed-ability games and scene practice.
Course teaching improvised musical theatre/singing scenes; no prior singing experience needed.
Adjacent courses teaching stand-up comedy and sketch comedy writing/performance alongside the improv ladder.
Course applying improv principles (spontaneity, presence, listening) to public-speaking confidence.

exercise_name: Humor Writing Level I — Secret formula of humor
description: Week 1 of the 10-week Humor Writing workshop: learn the underlying 'formula' to all humor, survey prose humor forms (fiction, nonfiction, in-between), and learn where to find humorous ideas; paired with a writing exercise.
Week 2 exercise practicing specific comedic techniques: exaggeration, juxtaposition, shock/surprise, extreme situations, sound/rhythm/wordplay, irony, attitude, and absurdity.

exercise_name: Humor Writing — Structure exercise (rule of three, snowballing)
description: Week 4 exercise applying structural humor techniques: the rule of three, snowballing, finding a major dramatic question, and shaping a beginning/middle/end.

exercise_name: Humor Writing — Point of view & comic voice
description: Week 5 exercise exploring types of POV and voice and finding your own comic voice through writing.
Weeks 6-7 exercises on funny description (using the senses, specificity) and comic dialogue/scene-writing.

exercise_name: Humor Writing — Workshop critique (present work twice)
description: Across the 10 weeks each student submits original humor pieces and has work critiqued by the class twice; lectures + exercises + peer workshopping.
Condensed one-day version of the humor-writing fundamentals with in-class writing exercises.

exercise_name: Stand-Up Comedy Writing — 'What is a joke?' analysis
description: Week 1 of the 10-week stand-up course: dissect a joke into subject/point of view/twist and information-part/funny-part; analyze existing jokes.

exercise_name: Stand-Up — 'Ways to improve a joke' editing drills
description: Weeks 3-4 exercises: editing, repetition, shock, choosing the best words, joke dissection, adapting to circumstance, and adding relevance to punch up jokes.

exercise_name: Stand-Up — Discover and communicate your comic persona
description: Week 6-7 exercises on finding your stage persona, timing, and finding out what others think is funny about you.

exercise_name: Stand-Up — Build and perform a 5-minute set
description: Course culminates in assembling a five-minute stand-up set, rehearsing it, and optionally performing it at an NYC comedy club on class night.
Breathing exercises used as the foundation for vocal power and steadiness before speaking, drawn from actor training.
Vocal exercises to develop range, resonance, and projection so the voice can carry the speech.
Non-verbal/physical performance exercise (gesture, posture, presence) to communicate before speaking.
Structured exercise to surface and then narrow a speech's single 'big idea' and turn it into a promise to the audience.
Delivery exercise creating dynamic contrast (pace, volume, energy, tone) within a speech to keep an audience engaged.
Storytelling exercise building a talk's narrative using three-act structure, then outlining the story beat by beat.
Rehearsal technique that maps the content/flow of the speech so the performer knows the shape and transitions cold.
Actor-derived rehearsal drill marking 'beats' and identifying the operative (most important) words in each line to control emphasis.
Flagship grad program where speakers learn to block and stage their specific speech, drilling small sections in a rehearsal lab until each is nailed.
Grad program teaching a repeatable process to create, build, and script an 'ovation-worthy' keynote from zero to stage, with feedback loops and group accountability.
Live coaching segments where individual students perform their speech and are guided through it on the spot by Michael and Amy Port.
Vocal/face warm-up: open the mouth wide like a lion then scrunch the face tiny like a mouse, repeated ~5 times, to loosen the articulators before speaking.

exercise_name: Humming warm-up / hum on a scale
description: Vocal-cord warm-up: hum for a stretch, then hum low-to-high-to-low on a scale to warm and place the voice.
Articulation exercise to over-enunciate and move the mouth so words land with clarity and 'executive presence'.
Delivery drill practicing deliberate silent pauses for emphasis and to slow a rushed speaker.
Body-and-breath exercises to project the voice and speak with vocal authority; framed as the 'M = Move Your Mouth / project' set of the Moxie method.

exercise_name: Speak With Moxie Masterclass — write an unforgettable speech
description: Masterclass module that walks the speaker from outline to final draft of a memorable speech (one of the 10 core speaker skills taught).

exercise_name: Speak With Moxie Masterclass — 5 keys to fear(less) / pre-show ritual
description: Module teaching performer tools to resolve doubt and stage fear: the '5 keys to fear(less)', creating a pre-show ritual, and 'owning the room'.

exercise_name: Speak With Moxie Masterclass — use your whole body for authority
description: Performance-based module teaching how to use the whole body (movement, posture, gesture) to project authority while speaking.
Professional 1:1 presentation coaching where a speaker's delivery (voice, body, narrative) is coached and refined, including for individuals and teams.
Session 1B activity: practice memory methods and play a name-recall game to learn and use every participant's name, creating positive first impressions.
Session 2B: prepare and deliver a two-minute talk about a specific defining moment from your life/career, using experience to build confident, clear, concise speaking.
Session 3B: deliver a two-minute report on a deliberate breakthrough achievement while bringing a physical prop/exhibit that illustrates it (show-and-tell talk).
Session 3A interpersonal drill practicing a confident, enthusiastic handshake / greeting.
Session 4A activity used in the 'put stress in perspective' session to demonstrate principles for handling stress.
Session 5A energizing activity: an action-oriented exercise that adds physical action/animation to communication to release nervous energy and become more natural.

exercise_name: I Know People exercise (Unleash Full Potential)
description: Session 5B: deliver a one-minute Magic-Formula talk on a topic of strong conviction to display courage, confidence, and become more convincing.

exercise_name: Duke of Kroy / Make Ideas Clear talk
description: Session 6A: deliver a two-minute report teaching the group something you do at work (using the LIONS formula) plus a prop, practicing clear logical sequencing; paired with the 'Duke of Kroy' exercise.
Session 6B: impromptu-speaking activity where participants speak with clarity and conviction in unscripted situations (no prep allowed).
Session 7A activity supporting the 'gain willing cooperation' lesson on influencing through trust, plus a two-minute application report.

exercise_name: Awake! Alert! Alive! + Power of Recognition
description: Session 8A energizing exercise plus a recognition activity practicing giving and receiving sincere, strength-centered feedback in small groups.

exercise_name: Two Speaking at Once / Disagree Agreeably
description: Session 10A: impromptu exercise (including a 'two speaking at once' drill) practicing organizing thoughts on the fly, cushioning, and using evidence (DEFEATS) to disagree without conflict.
Session 11B: deliver a two-minute talk about an event or person that had a strong emotional impact on you, practicing connecting with an audience emotionally.

Recurring core mechanic across all 12 sessions: each session participants prepare and deliver a short (60-120s) talk applying that week's principle, many structured by the 'Magic Formula' (incident-action-benefit), with coaching/feedback after each.

Core program: group classes (typically 3) led by Stephen Rosenfield and staff teaching writing and performing techniques to develop each student's unique comedic voice (no fill-in-the-blank formulas).

exercise_name: Private writing sessions with Stephen Rosenfield
description: One-on-one private sessions (typically 2) where the student works directly with Rosenfield to make their material funnier and more original.
Workshop culminates in a live stand-up performance at Gotham Comedy Club or West Side Comedy Club (or a nationally streamed online show) where students perform their written, rehearsed set.
Compressed intensive format running the full write-rehearse-perform arc over five consecutive days (also offered online).
Specialty workshop teaching students to mine personal stories and shape them into stand-up material.

exercise_name: Acting in Sitcoms, Movies and Theater Comedies
description: Specialty workshop teaching comedic acting/performance for screen and stage comedy.
Workshop (offered notably via college/university programs) teaching writing and performing sketch comedy.
1:1 coaching for beginners through pros covering writing/performance enhancement, audition prep, speech refinement, and performance readiness.
